questions.grammar_rule: Use 'on' for days of the week
questions.explanation: Days of the week always use 'on' (on Monday, on Tuesday, etc.)

questions.grammar_rule: Use 'at' for specific times
questions.explanation: Specific clock times use 'at' (at 7 o'clock, at noon, at midnight)

questions.grammar_rule: Use 'in' for years, months, and seasons
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Yillar, oylar va fasllar bilan 'in' ishlatiladi
questions.explanation: Years, months, and longer periods use 'in' (in 1995, in January, in summer)

questions.grammar_rule: Use 'on' for surfaces
questions.explanation: 'On' is used when something is touching a surface

questions.grammar_rule: Use 'in' for enclosed spaces
questions.explanation: 'In' shows something is inside an enclosed space

questions.grammar_rule: Use 'on' for streets, 'in' for towns/cities/countries
questions.explanation: Streets use 'on' (on Main Street), but cities use 'in' (in New York)

questions.sentence: She is waiting ___ the bus stop.
questions.grammar_rule: Use 'at' for specific points or locations
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Aniq nuqta yoki joy uchun 'at' ishlatiladi
questions.explanation: 'At' is used for specific points (at the bus stop, at the door)

questions.grammar_rule: Use 'at' for holidays and special occasions
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Bayramlar va maxsus kunlar uchun 'at' ishlatiladi
questions.explanation: Holidays use 'at' (at Christmas, at Easter, at New Year)

questions.grammar_rule: 'Through' means passing from one side to the other inside something
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Through' biror narsa ichidan bir tomondan ikkinchi tomonga o'tishni bildiradi
questions.explanation: 'Through' is used for three-dimensional movement inside something

questions.grammar_rule: 'Across' means from one side to the other on a surface
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Across' sirt bo'ylab bir tomondan ikkinchisiga o'tishni bildiradi
questions.explanation: 'Across' is for movement over a surface from one side to the other

questions.grammar_rule: 'Good at' is the correct collocation for skills/subjects
questions.grammar_rule_uz: Malaka va fanlar uchun 'good at' to'g'ri birikma
questions.explanation: We say 'good at + subject/skill', not 'good in'

questions.correct_answer: The movie starts at 8 PM on Friday.
questions.grammar_rule: 'At' for specific times, 'on' for days
questions.explanation: Specific time = at; day of week = on

questions.sentence: He succeeded ___ spite of the difficulties.
questions.grammar_rule: 'In spite of' is a fixed phrase meaning 'despite'
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'In spite of' - 'qaramay' degan ma'noni beruvchi qo'shma ibora
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is an idiomatic expression meaning 'despite'

questions.sentence: I'm not used ___ waking up early.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Be used to + verb-ing' means be accustomed to
questions.grammar_rule_uz: 'Be used to + verb-ing' o'rganib qolganlikni bildiradi
questions.explanation: 'Be used to' is followed by a noun or gerund, meaning 'be accustomed to'

questions.sentence: She complained about the noise to the manager.
questions.correct_answer: She complained about the noise to the manager.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Complain about something to someone' is correct
questions.explanation: This sentence is actually correct! 'Complain about something to someone'

questions.sentence: The solution ___ the problem was simple.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Solution to' is the correct collocation
questions.explanation: We say 'solution to a problem', not 'solution of' or 'solution for'

questions.sentence: She apologized ___ being late ___ the meeting.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Apologize for + action/thing' and 'apologize to + person'
questions.explanation: 'Apologize for doing something', 'apologize to a person', but 'for the meeting' is the action

questions.sentence: He was accused ___ stealing the money.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Accused of' is the correct legal/formal collocation
questions.explanation: 'Accuse someone of doing something' is the correct structure

questions.original_sentence: She insisted in paying for the dinner.
questions.correct_answer: She insisted on paying for the dinner.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Insist on' is the correct collocation
questions.explanation: 'Insist on doing something', not 'insist in'

questions.sentence: The increase of prices affected everyone.
questions.correct_answer: The increase in prices affected everyone.
questions.grammar_rule: 'Increase/decrease in' is the correct collocation
questions.explanation: We say 'increase in' something, not 'increase of'
